summary: The petitioners, candidates who participated in NEET-PG-2021 counselling but remained unallocated, sought a Special Stray Round of counselling for 1,456 remaining vacant seats. They argued that the seats, including clinical ones, must be filled to prevent wastage and that merit-based admissions for 2021 candidates should continue. Respondents, including the Union of India and Medical Counselling Committee, opposed, stating that four rounds (including stray vacancy) had already been conducted, most vacancies were in non-clinical or high-fee private courses unlikely to be filled, and admissions for NEET-PG-2022 were underway. The Court considered disruption to academic schedules and prior counselling rounds but no final order is stated in the excerpt.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 32 of the Constitution of India
final_judgment: Disposed of by a common order; specific relief not granted in the provided text.
